blocks.html: Funnel Leakage refers to the loss of prospects at various stages of the sales or marketing funnel due to disengagement, poor qualification, ineffective follow-up, or process inefficiencies.

Funnel Leakage occurs when potential customers drop out before completing the buyer journey, reducing overall conversion rates and impacting revenue growth. It can happen at any stage of the funnel, from initial lead generation to final deal closure. Identifying where leakage happens helps businesses improve performance and optimize their sales and marketing strategies.
Funnel leakage is typically analyzed by reviewing conversion rates between funnel stages, such as:

items.html: Leads generated to marketing qualified leads (MQLs)
Complex buying processes or pricing concerns

blocks.html: Increases return on marketing and sales investments

A company generates 1,000 leads per month, but only 50 become qualified opportunities because many leads are not contacted quickly enough. This drop-off indicates significant funnel leakage in the follow-up stage.

Funnel Leakage is a critical metric for evaluating sales and marketing performance. By identifying where prospects are lost and addressing the root causes, businesses can strengthen their funnel, improve conversions, and maximize revenue potential.
